claims.text: Computationally guided annealing will induce selective surface enrichment of Pd in the near-equiatomic multi-principal-element alloy catalyst.
Pd surface enrichment will improve low-temperature oxidation activity.
Pd surface enrichment will enhance resistance to typical exhaust poisons.
Pd surface enrichment will extend catalyst lifetime.
The annealing treatment will form Pd-enriched nanoclusters on the catalyst surface.
The annealing treatment will preserve a stable multi-principal-element bulk structure.
Pd-enriched surface clusters will act as highly active oxidation sites.
Pd-enriched surface clusters will provide improved tolerance to H2O and NO poisoning.
The multi-principal-element bulk structure will provide long-term thermal stability.
The multi-principal-element bulk structure will resist catalyst degradation.
The annealed catalyst will have a lower CO and hydrocarbon oxidation onset temperature than the unmodified catalyst.
The annealed catalyst will retain higher conversion efficiency in the presence of H2O and NO than the unmodified catalyst.
The annealed catalyst will degrade more slowly during accelerated aging than the unmodified catalyst.
The treatment will produce the predicted improvements without significantly increasing total platinum-group-metal usage.
The predicted benefits apply under transient exhaust operation below 150 °C containing CO, hydrocarbons, H2O, and NO.
Accelerated aging protocols can mimic vehicle-lifetime mileage for testing the proposed durability benefit.
